Select the top-sensitivity panel at 90% specificity.

Source: R/panel_summarization.R
select_panel_top_sensitivity.Rd

Given solution-level performance summaries this function identifies the panel that maximises external sensitivity while constraining the loss relative to internal cross-validation performance.

select_panel_top_sensitivity(
  performance,
  solution_col = "solution_id",
  external_col = "external_sens_at_spec90",
  internal_col = "internal_sens_at_spec90",
  max_loss = Inf,
  panel_size_col = NULL
)

Arguments

performance

Data frame where each row summarises a solution. Must contain at minimum columns referenced by solution_col, external_col, and internal_col.

solution_col

Column name holding the solution_id.

external_col

Column name holding sensitivity at 90% specificity for the external validation cohort.

internal_col

Column name holding the corresponding internal cross-validation sensitivity.

max_loss

Maximum allowable drop in sensitivity between internal and external evaluations (internal - external). Defaults to Inf.

panel_size_col

Optional column containing the number of biomarkers in each solution. Used purely as a tie-breaker (smaller panels preferred).

Value

A single-row data frame describing the selected solution. An extra column named performance_loss (internal minus external sensitivity) is appended for convenience. Returns NULL if no solution satisfies max_loss or if required columns are missing.
